title: Academy Award Theater
paragraphs: A Hollywood anthology that adapted notable motion pictures for radio, often bringing film stars back to recreate their screen roles in condensed dramatic form.

Complete 39-program CBS Hollywood anthology adapting prominent motion pictures and source stories/plays for radio. Two frozen dates are corrected additively: White Cliffs of Dover to Sep. 18 and Guest in the House to Sep. 25.

GRH documents the program through Saturday CBS run (March 30, 1946 to June 29, 1946) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Wednesday CBS run (July 3, 1946 to December 18, 1946) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Dee Englebach (director on 39 recordings and producer on 39 recordings), Frank Wilson (radio adaptor on 39 recordings, narrator on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording), Hugh Brundage (announcer on 39 recordings and host on 1 recording), Leith Stevens (composer on 39 recordings and conductor on 39 recordings), [[person|jeff-chandler|Jeff Chandler]] (performer on 2 recordings), Joan Lorring (performer on 2 recordings), and John Garfield (performer on 2 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Hollywood motion-picture adaptation for radio, Academy Award and prestige-film culture, romance and relationship drama, war, anti-fascism and wartime experience, comedy and social satire, and crime, mystery and suspense.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Hollywood films and prestige stories adapted for network radio, Postwar Hollywood prestige culture, Squibb-sponsored prestige anthology, and Saturday-to-Wednesday schedule move.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (60 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (25 shared credited people), [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]] (12 shared credited people), [[show|screen-guild-theater|Screen Guild Theater]] (9 shared credited people), and [[show|old-gold-comedy-theater|Old Gold Comedy Theater]] (7 shared credited people).
